2 You are provided with two solid salts, solid E and solid F.
Do the following tests on solid E and solid F, recording all of your observations at each stage.
tests on solid E

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the appearance of solid E.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Place about half of solid E in a hard glass test-tube. Heat the solid gently then strongly.
Record your observations.

Add the rest of solid E to about 10cm of distilled water in a boiling tube. Stopper the boiling tube
and shake it to dissolve solid E and form solution E.
Divide solution E into three approximately equal portions in three test-tubes.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Add a few drops of dilute nitric acid and about 1cm of aqueous silver nitrate to the first portion
of solution E.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Add a few drops of dilute nitric acid and about 1cm of aqueous barium nitrate to the second
portion of solution E.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Add an excess of aqueous sodium hydroxide to the third portion of solution E.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
Identify solid E.

tests on solid F
Add solid F to about 10cm of distilled water in a boiling tube. Stopper the boiling tube and shake
it to dissolve solid F and form solution F.
Divide solution F into three approximately equal portions in three test-tubes.

parts.label: (g)
parts.text:
Test the pH of the first portion of solution F.
pH = ______

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Add a few drops of aqueous sodium hydroxide to the second portion of solution F and
shake the mixture.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Now add an excess of aqueous sodium hydroxide to the mixture.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Add an excess of aqueous ammonia to the third portion of solution F.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (j)
parts.text:
What conclusion can you draw about the cation present in solid F?
